business-data-context

Business data map

What the system under test (tuDeclaracion.com) is at the data level: entities and why they exist, business flows, state machines, automatic processes and integrations. Schema read from the repository migrations, not from the live database.

Overview

tuDeclaracion keeps very little data: the accountant's monthly accounting lines, a few rules per client company, and one status flag per declaration. The PADI files the accountant finally downloads (DJ 2181 and DJ 1376) are not stored. They are recomputed from the stored lines and rules every time a review page opens (Server Component) and the file text is built in the browser at download. A status flag only records that a download happened once.

Everything hangs from one tenant chain: a cuenta (the accountant's login) owns many empresa rows (client companies), and each empresa owns its rules (plan_cuentas, mapeo_1376) and its monthly data (declaracion, asiento, declaracion_1376). Row Level Security on every one of those tables scopes access through empresa.cuenta_id = auth.uid(). Almost all reads and writes go straight from the browser to Supabase under the user's own session. Server-side code is limited to a few Server Actions, two auth route handlers and the review pages.

Actor or systemRole in the dataFound in
AccountantThe only human role. Owns one cuenta, many empresas. No admin or second role exists in the schema.supabase/migrations/20260712000000_baseline_cuenta_empresa.sql
Supabase AuthHolds identities in auth.users; a trigger mirrors each new user into cuenta; an auth hook sends every auth email.20260712000000_baseline_cuenta_empresa.sql, supabase/functions/send-email/
BCU web serviceSource of the USD exchange rate. Fetched only by the server and cached in a table shared by every tenant.src/modules/cotizacion/
DGI and PADIOffline destination. The accountant imports the downloaded text file into PADI by hand; the app never talks to DGI.src/modules/exporter/

Size of the model: 9 business tables, 5 RPC functions (insertar_asientos, crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, guardar_mapeo_1376, borrar_periodo), 3 triggers, 0 cron jobs and 1 webhook (the auth Send Email hook). Every figure comes from the migrations in ../tudeclaracion/supabase/migrations/, not from the live database (see discovery-gaps).

Entities

EntityBusiness roleWhy it exists
cuentaThe accountant's login and display name. One per Supabase Auth user, created automatically at sign-up.Root of tenant isolation: every business row is reachable only through the cuenta that owns its empresa.
empresaA client company the accountant files for. Identified by a 12-digit RUT, unique inside one cuenta.Everything a declaration needs hangs from it. It is also the unit the user "enters" (the active company).
plan_cuentasThe company's own rules: which accounting account (and, for quick-format lines, which IVA code digit) means which PADI code, tagged as belonging to the 2181 or to the 1376.Tax rules are data per company, not code. Each accountant's chart of accounts differs.
codigo_linea_1376The fixed list of 1376 line codes (10 rows, seeded provisionally). Read-only for users.Skeleton of the 1376 mapping screen and of the 1376 output.
mapeo_1376Per company, which account (and optional IVA code) feeds each 1376 line, and from which side (Debe or Haber).The 1376 totals are sums of accounting movements; this table says which movements count for which line.
declaracionOne company's 2181 for one month. Owns that month's accounting lines and carries the 2181 status.Gives imported lines a period and a status. It is created by the import, not by the user.
declaracion_1376One company's 1376 for the same month. Status only.The 1376 reuses the 2181's lines (same monthly TXT) but needs its own status.
asientoOne accounting line imported from the monthly TXT, kept as imported.Single raw input of both engines, stored once per period.
cotizacion_bcu_cacheDaily USD rate published by BCU, one row per currency code and date, shared by every tenant.Avoids calling BCU per line and holds the rate DGI requires (previous business day).
auth.users (platform)Supabase's own identity table. Not a business table.Source of cuenta.id; deleting a user cascades to cuenta and everything below.

Relationships. One cuenta has many empresas; one empresa has many plan_cuentas, mapeo_1376, declaracion, declaracion_1376 and asiento rows; one declaracion has many asiento rows. All of these are on delete cascade, so removing an empresa removes its whole history. mapeo_1376.codigo_linea references codigo_linea_1376 without cascade. declaracion and declaracion_1376 are not linked by a foreign key: they match only through (empresa_id, periodo). cotizacion_bcu_cache and codigo_linea_1376 belong to no tenant.

Uniqueness rules that shape behaviour: one empresa per (cuenta_id, rut); one declaration per (empresa_id, periodo) in each of the two declaration tables; in plan_cuentas, one row per (empresa_id, cuenta_contable) and one per (empresa_id, codigo_iva) (several rows may have no IVA code); in mapeo_1376, one row per (empresa_id, codigo_linea), per (empresa_id, cuenta_contable) and per (empresa_id, codigo_iva).

The generated types file lists three more tables, declarations, data_fields and declaration_required_fields, that no migration creates and no code reads. They are not documented here as entities (see discovery-gaps).

Entity: asiento

An asiento is one line of the accountant's monthly TXT, exactly as imported. Two things are easy to misread. First, debe and haber hold accounting account codes, not amounts; the amounts are total and iva. Second, one logical accounting entry can arrive as several rows (an "asiento abierto" is split across lines), so a row is not a business transaction on its own.

  • Each row belongs to one declaracion (the month) and also carries empresa_id directly. The period is set by the import, not read from the file.
  • Rows are write-once: the table has select, insert and delete policies and no update policy. Re-importing a period deletes and re-inserts.
  • Database checks repeat the parser's rules because the import RPC can be called without the app: day 1 to 31, Debe and Haber digits or empty (never both empty), non-empty concepto, currency 0 or 1, IVA code 0 to 9, Libro in C, V, E, I, P.
  • tipo may be null, 504 or any value containing a letter (the engines ignore the lettered ones). A numeric Tipo other than 504 is turned into null by the parser before saving.
  • The 12-digit RUT check was dropped from the table (ADR-0008): the RUT matters only for lines the 2181 resolves, so the parser checks it on those lines and the 2181 engine excludes any resolved line with a bad RUT. The column stays NOT NULL.
  • There is no uniqueness constraint on lines. Preventing a duplicate import depends entirely on the logic inside insertar_asientos. Rows keep no reference to the source file or line number.
  • For dollar lines (moneda = 1) the stored cotizacion is the rate that was used: the one in the TXT, or the BCU rate resolved at import when the TXT carried 0.

Entity: plan_cuentas

The per-company dictionary that turns accounting vocabulary into PADI vocabulary. Each row says: "this account number (and optionally this IVA code digit) means PADI code X, for declaration 2181 or 1376". It was redesigned on 2026-07-15 from a fixed five-row catalog into free data the user types, because several accounts can resolve to the same PADI code and the code digits are the accountant's own.

  • 2181 rows use PADI codes 502 to 506 (sales and purchases VAT, exempt purchases). 1376 rows use the line codes of codigo_linea_1376. Some codes (for example 502) exist in both catalogs with different meaning, which is why each row stores declaracion (ADR-0007). Each engine reads only its own rows.
  • Exempt-purchase accounts (PADI 504) carry no IVA code and match only by account. They are the rows where several lines may share an empty IVA code.
  • codigo_padi is free text: its CHECK was removed so the 1376 codes could be stored. The only guard is the dropdown in the app.
  • The account prefix matters: an account starting with 1 is treated as purchase-side, starting with 2 as sales-side, and is cross-checked against the line's Libro.
  • Saved only through crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas and editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas (delete everything, then re-insert, in one transaction). A request of more than 2000 rows is rejected.
  • Because both unique constraints ignore declaracion, one account number or one IVA code cannot appear in a 2181 row and also in a 1376 row of the same company (inferred from the constraints; UI behaviour not verified).
  • Editing the plan does not touch lines already imported, and does not reset any status. The engines apply the new plan the next time a period is opened.

Entity: mapeo_1376 and codigo_linea_1376

The 1376 declares totals per line code, not per RUT. codigo_linea_1376 is the fixed skeleton (10 codes: 101, 102, 103, 201, 301, 302, 501, 502, 510, 601, each with a concept and an order). mapeo_1376 is the company's answer to "which accounting movements make up each line".

  • The relation is one-to-one in both directions: a line code takes at most one account, and an account feeds at most one line code. Both are enforced by unique constraints and by the screen's own validation.
  • Each row records the side to read (Debe or Haber) and an optional IVA code digit 1 to 9. Without an IVA code the row only collects open-format entries. With one, quick-format movements with that code also feed the line (ADR-0010). A column "which amount to use" existed before 2026-10-15 and was dropped.
  • The catalog is a provisional seed built from a spreadsheet the user supplied; the official DGI list had not been captured when it was written. It is meant to be replaced as data, without code changes.
  • Users can only read the catalog (no insert, update or delete policy). Maintenance is meant for a back office that does not exist yet.
  • Saved through guardar_mapeo_1376 (ownership check, delete everything, re-insert; at most 500 rows). A duplicate account or IVA code makes the whole save fail and roll back.

Entity: declaracion and declaracion_1376 (the period)

There is no "period" table. A period is the pair (empresa_id, periodo) written AAAAMM (for example 202506), and it exists as soon as a declaracion row exists. The dashboard builds one row per period by joining the two tables in application code (armarPeriodos): a period is "Completo" when both statuses are generada. That completeness is never stored.

  • declaracion (the 2181) owns the imported lines and is created by the import, including when the user chose to import for the 1376.
  • declaracion_1376 owns only a status. It is created the first time someone opens the 1376 review page for a period that has lines (a page load that writes). If the row is missing the dashboard shows the 1376 as pending.
  • The statuses are not typed by the user. They change only through the import RPC and the two download buttons (see the two state- sections).
  • Deleting a period removes both rows and, by cascade, all its lines. The empresa, its plan and its 1376 mapping stay.

Entity: cotizacion_bcu_cache

A shared lookup of public BCU data, not tenant data: key (moneda_codigo, fecha), value the rate. The code uses a single currency code, 2230 ("dólar interbancario fondo"). It started as one latest value per currency and became a daily history on 2026-07-28 so a line can be priced at the business day before its own date.

  • Any authenticated user can read it. Since 2026-10-02 only the server can write it, through the secret-key admin client that bypasses RLS, because any user could previously insert rows and poison the rate used in other tenants' declarations (threat-model item 5).
  • The Server Actions that write it check for a logged-in session themselves, since RLS no longer does.
  • The sidebar card and the "Cotizaciones" page read the same table. The card is meant to fall back to the last stored value when BCU is unreachable, but its fallback query takes one row without ordering or limit from a table that now holds one row per day (see discovery-gaps).

Flow: account access (sign-up, login, recovery, logout)

An accountant creates a login, proves the email, signs in with password or Google, and can recover a lost password. The only data written by this flow is the cuenta row.

Sign-up and email confirmation

  1. The browser calls Supabase Auth signUp with email and password, an optional Turnstile captcha token and emailRedirectTo = /auth/confirm?next=/inicio.
  2. Auth inserts the user in auth.users. The trigger on_auth_user_created runs handle_new_user and inserts the matching cuenta (id, email). The browser could not do this itself: users have no insert policy on cuenta.
  3. When the Send Email hook is enabled (see integration-resend-email), Auth calls it; the accountant receives a link to /auth/confirm?token_hash=...&type=...&redirect_to=....
  4. /auth/confirm calls verifyOtp; on success it redirects to next (default /inicio), on failure to /login?error=verification-failed (or /forgot-password?error=expired for recovery).

Login

  1. Password login uses signInWithPassword with the optional captcha token. Google login uses signInWithOAuth and lands on /auth/callback, which exchanges the code for a session.
  2. After a Google login, if cuenta.nombre is empty it is filled from the Google profile name (trimmed to 80 characters). A name the user already set is never overwritten.
  3. Supabase links a Google identity to an existing password account by verified email instead of creating a second account.

Recovery and logout

  1. Forgot-password calls resetPasswordForEmail with redirectTo = /auth/confirm?type=recovery&next=/reset-password. The confirm route opens a recovery session and /reset-password calls updateUser({ password }).
  2. Logout (salir Server Action) signs out and deletes the empresa_activa_id cookie so the next person on the machine does not inherit the active company; it redirects to /login even when sign-out fails.

Business rules:

  • Middleware refreshes the session on every request. Without a user, /inicio, /cuenta, /empresas and /dashboard redirect to /login?redirect=.... A logged-in user visiting /login, /signup or /forgot-password goes to /inicio. /reset-password is deliberately not redirected.
  • The post-login next value must be a same-origin path; anything else falls back to /inicio (open-redirect guard).
  • The captcha widget is shown only when its site key is configured; whether Supabase enforces it server-side is not visible in the repository.

Flow: create and edit a client company

Before any declaration exists, the accountant registers each client company and teaches the app how that company's accounts map to PADI codes.

  1. On /empresas/nueva the accountant enters the RUT (digits only, exactly 12), the name, a list of rows "account number, IVA code digit, PADI code" (each PADI option is tagged 2181 or 1376) and a list of exempt-purchase accounts (PADI 504).
  2. The browser calls crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas. In one transaction it inserts the empresa under auth.uid() and all plan_cuentas rows. A failure leaves nothing behind, so a company never exists with a half-saved plan.
  3. A duplicate RUT in the same cuenta raises unique violation 23505 on empresa_cuenta_rut_unique, shown as "RUT already exists". The same code is also raised by the two unique constraints of plan_cuentas; the constraint name tells them apart.
  4. On /empresas the accountant picks the active company. The Server Action seleccionarEmpresaActiva stores its id in the httpOnly cookie empresa_activa_id (30 days). If the cookie is missing or points to a company the user does not own, the most recently created company is used.
  5. Editing (/empresas/[id]) calls editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas: update name and RUT, check the update touched a row (RLS makes a foreign id update zero rows, so the function raises an explicit error), delete every plan row and re-insert the submitted ones.

Business rules:

  • RUT format is enforced twice: in the form and by the database CHECK (12 digits). The RUT is not checked against DGI: any 12 digits are accepted.
  • Both RPCs reject more than 2000 plan rows. Every IVA row needs an account and an IVA code; exempt rows need only an account.
  • Editing a company's plan changes how already imported periods resolve the next time they are opened. No status is reset and no warning is raised.
  • No screen deletes an empresa, although the delete policy and the cascade exist.

Flow: import a monthly TXT

The accountant uploads the TXT exported from the accounting software for one month. This is the only way period data enters the system and it writes declaracion and asiento in one transaction.

  1. On the dashboard the accountant chooses the declaration type (2181 or 1376), picks the month (AAAA-MM, stored as AAAAMM) and the file. If the file has more than the standard columns, the user first declares which of nine optional extra columns it carries; those are ignored but occupy positions.
  2. The browser loads the active company's 2181 plan rows and parses the file locally. With a header row, only the 1376 import reads columns by title (ADR-0009); the 2181 import reads by position.
  3. Parsing validates every line and reports all invalid fields of the failing line at once. If any line fails, the whole file is rejected and nothing is saved.
  4. If any dollar line has rate 0 in the TXT, a Server Action fills cotizacion_bcu_cache for the month and each such line is priced at the last rate strictly before its own day. If a rate cannot be found, the import stops with a "rate not available" message.
  5. The browser calls insertar_asientos(empresa, periodo, lineas, reemplazar). If the period already has lines and replace was not chosen, it raises periodo_ya_procesado; the dialog asks the user to confirm replacing first. More than 20000 lines raise demasiadas_lineas.
  6. With replace, the old lines are deleted. In every case the declaracion row is created or reset to abierta and the new lines are inserted in the same transaction. For a 1376 import the screen then opens the 1376 review.

Business rules:

  • All-or-nothing: one bad field rejects the whole file; a failed insert writes nothing.
  • A line with a RUT that is not 12 digits is rejected only if the 2181 would resolve it (Tipo 504, or its IVA code or account is in the plan). Other lines may carry any RUT value.
  • A Libro that disagrees with the account prefix no longer rejects the file (2026-10-26): the line is imported and the 2181 engine excludes it with a reason.
  • Cotización accepts 0 or two integer digits with any number of decimals; the raw bank precision is kept and rounding happens later.
  • A Tipo with letters is accepted; a numeric Tipo other than 504 is silently turned into empty.
  • Importing for the 1376 also writes the 2181's declaracion row: both declarations of a month share the same lines.

Flow: review and download the 2181

The 2181 declares purchases and sales detail per third-party RUT. Opening /dashboard/declaraciones/[periodo] loads the period's lines and the company's 2181 plan rows, resolves every line live, and shows what will and will not be in the file. Nothing computed is saved.

  1. For every line, in this order: a Tipo with letters is excluded as out of scope. Tipo 504 resolves to code 504 using the Total column. Otherwise, if Código IVA is above 0, the plan row with that IVA code is used and the amount is the IVA column ("Camino 1"). Otherwise (open entry, Código IVA 0) the Debe account is tried first, then Haber, against the plan; the amount is the Total column ("Camino 2").
  2. Dollar amounts are multiplied by the line's cotización and rounded to a whole peso with a half-down rule (a fraction up to .50 truncates, above .50 rounds up).
  3. Lines are then excluded, with a reason shown to the accountant, when: no plan row matches (sin-mapeo), the account prefix and Libro disagree (libro-inconsistente or codigo-iva-libro-inconsistente), the converted amount is 0 (importe-invalido), or the RUT is not 12 digits (rut-invalido). Counterpart lines of an open entry that already resolved through another line of the same day, concept, Libro and RUT are not reported.
  4. Resolved lines are summed per RUT and PADI code. Negative lines (credit notes) net against positive ones; any group whose net is 0 or negative is dropped and listed as "no positive balance".
  5. The Download button builds the file in the browser: seven fields separated by ;, one line per group, no header, each line ending in ;: declarant RUT, form number 02181, period, third-party RUT, period, PADI code, amount as an integer padded to 12 digits. File name 2181_{rut}_{periodo}.txt.
  6. After the first download the browser sets declaracion.estado = generada directly (see state-declaracion).

Business rules:

  • Final amounts round at two decimals against 0.50: up to .50 goes down, from .51 goes up (a different half-down rule from the dollar conversion).
  • The download is available whenever the period has lines, even if some lines were excluded; the screen only warns ("N exclusions ... not included in the PADI file").
  • Only lines resolve; the exclusions are computed, never stored, so reopening the page after editing the plan can change the result.
  • An asiento with a negative Total or IVA triggers an extra warning that the file may contain empty lines.

Flow: configure the 1376 mapping

Before a 1376 can show totals, the accountant tells the app which accounts feed each line code of the form.

  1. The screen lists the 10 catalog codes in order, one row each, with the saved assignment if any.
  2. For a code without a saved assignment, the company's 1376 plan rows whose PADI code equals the line code pre-fill the account and IVA code as a suggestion. The side (Debe or Haber) is never suggested because the plan does not record it.
  3. The accountant fills account, side and optionally an IVA code (1 to 9). A completely empty row is valid and means "this line gets nothing".
  4. Validation before saving: a row with data needs both account and side; IVA code must be 1 to 9; an account or an IVA code may not repeat across rows.
  5. The browser calls guardar_mapeo_1376 with only the completed rows. The function checks ownership, deletes the old mapping and re-inserts; a unique violation rolls everything back and the screen explains which constraint failed.

Saving a mapping does not change any stored line or status; the totals change the next time a period is opened.

Flow: review and download the 1376

The 1376 declares one total per line code. It reads the same stored lines as the 2181 but sums them through the company's 1376 mapping. Opening /dashboard/declaraciones-1376/[periodo] computes the totals live and, on first open with data, creates the declaracion_1376 row as abierta.

  1. Lines whose Tipo contains letters are ignored by this engine too (accountant rule of 2026-11-09).
  2. For each mapped line code, every remaining stored line contributes if it is a quick-format line (Código IVA above 0) whose IVA code equals the row's code (amount = IVA column), or an open-format line (Código IVA 0) whose Debe or Haber account, on the configured side, equals the row's account (amount = Total column). The line format decides the rule, so no movement counts twice.
  3. Dollar amounts convert with the line's cotización and the same half-down integer rounding; everything is summed with its sign (credit notes enter negative). A line code that no movement touches does not appear.
  4. The screen lists totals in catalog order. It also warns, without blocking, about accounts that the plan marks as 1376-relevant and moved in the period but are not in the mapping, and about quick-format IVA codes with movement that no mapping row collects (the accountant confirmed on 2026-10-21 that what is not mapped does not belong to the 1376).
  5. The Download button writes one line per code, code;amount, no header, no RUT or period. Each total rounds like the 2181 (up to .50 down, from .51 up). A code whose total is negative or rounds to 0 is not written. File name 1376_{periodo}.txt.
  6. After the first download the browser sets declaracion_1376.estado = generada.

Business rules:

  • No Libro cross-check, no per-line exclusion list and no RUT: the 1376 is a pure sum by mapping. A mistake in the mapping is invisible except through the totals.
  • A failure while loading or computing shows a guided error state instead of crashing the page.
  • The 1376 never reads the 2181 plan rows; it reads only rows tagged 1376 for the unmapped-account warning.

Flow: delete a period

From "Actividad reciente" the accountant can delete a whole month. This is the only user-facing delete in the product.

  1. The dashboard asks for confirmation, then calls borrar_periodo(empresa, periodo).
  2. In one transaction the function deletes the declaracion_1376 row, then the declaracion row; the foreign key cascade removes every asiento of the period.
  3. The company, its plan de cuentas and its 1376 mapping are untouched. On success the page refreshes; on failure a generic retry message is shown.

Business rules: the 2181 is the annex of the 1376 and both are computed from the same lines, so they are always deleted together. The function takes no ownership guard of its own: it relies on the delete policies of the two declaration tables (owner only).

Flow: USD exchange rate

Dollar lines need a rate to become pesos. DGI requires the rate of the business day before the line's date, never the same day.

  1. When a TXT has dollar lines with rate 0, the browser calls poblarCotizacionesBcuParaPeriodo. The Server Action requires a session, asks BCU (SOAP, currency 2230) for the range from 10 days before the month to the month end or yesterday, and upserts one row per business day through the admin client.
  2. Weekends and holidays do not appear in BCU's answer, so "the previous business day" is simply the latest cached date strictly before the line's day.
  3. Each such line is priced with that rate; a rate stored in the TXT always wins when it is not 0.
  4. Separately, the dashboard sidebar shows the latest rate. On load it fetches BCU and caches the value; if that fails it is meant to show the last cached value as a fallback, and an error with a retry button when there is none. By code the fallback query (maybeSingle without order or limit) can only succeed while the cache holds a single row for the currency, so with several cached days it likely returns the error state instead.

Failure behaviour: if BCU is down and no earlier rate is cached for the line, the import stops with a "rate not available" message and nothing is saved.

State: declaracion (2181)

declaracion.estado is a coarse progress flag, not the truth about the file. It allows three values, and the code reaches two of them.

FromToEventEffects
(none)abiertaFirst import of a period through insertar_asientos (2181 or 1376 import)Creates the row and inserts the lines atomically.
abiertageneradaThe accountant downloads the 2181 PADI fileThe browser runs an UPDATE (owner-only RLS policy). It only runs when the state is not already generada. If the UPDATE fails the file was already downloaded and a status error is shown.
generadaabiertaRe-import of the same period with replaceOld lines deleted, new lines inserted, status reset "to force regenerating".
abiertaabiertaRe-import with replaceSame replacement; status unchanged.
any(deleted)Delete period (borrar_periodo)Row and its lines removed together with the 1376 row.
anycon_erroresNo event found in codeThe CHECK allows it, nothing writes it. The "with warnings" badge on the review page is computed from exclusions at render time and never saved.

Rules:

  • Importing again without replace while the period has lines is blocked and changes nothing.
  • Downloading again after generada does not write anything.
  • The dashboard counts abierta as "pending to generate" and generada as generated; the home page counts only abierta 2181 rows as pending declarations (the 1376 is not included).
  • Editing the company's plan or mapping after generada does not change the status, although the recomputed file may no longer match what was downloaded.
  • updated_at has no trigger on this table (only cuenta and empresa have one) and the code never sets it, so by the migrations it stays at the creation time. The dashboard shows "last update" from this column.

State: declaracion_1376

Same two reachable values as the 2181 (abierta, generada; con_errores is allowed and never written) but with different lifecycle points.

FromToEventEffects
(none)abiertaFirst time the 1376 review page opens for a period that has linesThe server component inserts the row while rendering. A concurrent insert (unique violation) is re-read instead of failing.
abiertageneradaThe accountant downloads the 1376 fileBrowser UPDATE by (empresa_id, periodo). Unmapped-account warnings do not block the download.
generadageneradaRe-import of the period with replaceNo change. insertar_asientos resets only declaracion, so the 1376 can show generada over new lines.
any(deleted)Delete periodDeleted together with the 2181 row, first.

Rules:

  • No row means pending: the dashboard treats a missing row as abierta for the "Completo" check.
  • The 1376 review page refuses to compute and shows "no data yet" when the 2181 declaration or its lines are missing.
  • A period is "Completo" only when both declarations are generada.

State: empresa.estado

empresa.estado allows Pendiente (default) and Operativa, and the company list shows a badge from it, but no code path writes it: creating or editing a company never sets it, and no job or trigger does. By the code, every company shows "Pendiente". responsable and ultimo_movimiento are likewise never written, so the list shows an empty responsible and "Sin actividad reciente". Whether staging data was edited by hand to change them is unverified.

Supabase Auth Send Email hook to Edge Function send-emailEvery auth email (sign-up confirmation, password recovery)Verifies the Standard Webhooks signature with SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET, renders a Spanish email and sends it through Resend. 401 on a bad signature, 500 if Resend fails.Replaces Supabase's rate-limited test mailer (ADR-0002). Whether the hook is enabled on staging is not visible in the repository.

Integration: Resend (auth emails)

Data impact: none in the database. The email carries the one-time token_hash that lets /auth/confirm create a session. Dependent flows: account sign-up and password recovery (flow-account-access).

  • The function builds the link <site_url>/auth/confirm?token_hash=...&type=...&redirect_to=.... The confirm route never reads redirect_to; it reads next. Without next it redirects to /inicio. The pages that start recovery pass next=/reset-password inside Supabase's redirect URL, which the function forwards only as the encoded redirect_to. By code reading, a recovery link would land on /inicio instead of /reset-password (not run against staging).
  • Any action type other than recovery gets the sign-up confirmation text, including email change.
  • The sender is onboarding@resend.dev, Resend's shared test sender. Whether it delivers to arbitrary recipients on staging is unverified.
  • Failure behaviour: if the function or Resend fails, Auth cannot send the email, so the user never receives the confirmation or recovery link. The app shows no error for a lost email.

Integration: BCU exchange rate web service

Data in: daily USD rates through a SOAP call (cotizaciones.bcu.gub.uy, currency 2230, value TCC), made only by Server Actions and the dashboard server component because the service allows no browser CORS. Data out: nothing. Rows land in cotizacion_bcu_cache, written with the secret-key admin client.

  • Dependent flows: flow-import-period (dollar lines with rate 0) and flow-usd-rate.
  • The answer is parsed with regular expressions; a status other than 1 or a malformed body yields no rates.
  • Failure behaviour: the sidebar card is meant to fall back to the last cached rate (see flow-usd-rate for why that likely fails once several days are cached); an import that needs a rate with nothing cached before that day stops and saves nothing.

Integration: Google sign-in

Data in: an identity in auth.users (and from it a cuenta via the trigger) and the profile name, copied into cuenta.nombre once when it was empty. Dependent flow: flow-account-access. Failure behaviour: a denied consent screen or a failed code exchange returns to /login?error=google-auth-failed; no data is written. Identity linking by verified email is a Supabase behaviour, not code in this repository.

Integration: Cloudflare Turnstile captcha

Data impact: none stored. The widget produces a single-use token that sign-up, login and forgot-password pass to Supabase Auth as captchaToken. It only appears when its site key is configured, and the submit button stays disabled until a token exists. A captcha_failed answer is shown on login and recovery. Whether Supabase verifies the token (the [auth.captcha] block is commented out in the repo config) is unverified.

Discovery gaps

This map was generated without database access. The schema below comes from reading the 27 migrations in order and the code, not from the live staging database.

Not verified

  • Schema source: every table, constraint, policy and function in this map is reconstructed from ../tudeclaracion/supabase/migrations/. Whether every migration is applied on staging, and in that order, is unverified. The baseline migration states it was captured from the live DB on 2026-10-02, so earlier objects may differ.
  • Data distributions: which enum values are actually in use (Libro, Tipo, estado, moneda), row counts, and real periods per company are unknown. Only the current checks and defaults are known.
  • Three tables, declarations, data_fields and declaration_required_fields, appear in src/types/supabase.ts but no migration creates them and no code reads them. They probably exist in the live DB (or existed when the types were generated); purpose, data and RLS are unknown.
  • RLS and grants as actually deployed: policies were read from migrations only. The two catalog tables and the BCU cache allow select to any authenticated user; whether anonymous users can read anything is not confirmed.
  • The Send Email hook: whether it is enabled on staging, whether SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET is set, and which email templates and Site URL Supabase uses. supabase/config.toml holds local-only settings (email confirmations are disabled there) and configures neither the hook, the captcha nor the Google provider.
  • Whether Supabase enforces the Turnstile captcha server side.
  • Whether the TXT export used in staging tests matches the documented column order; only the app's own rules are known.
  • No source other than code was used for the business meaning of Libro values C, E, V, I, P (it comes from the app's SRS notes cited in the domain map).

Suspected defects and risks (verified in code, not reproduced)

  • Recovery redirect: the send-email function builds redirect_to but /auth/confirm reads next. By code, a recovery or sign-up link lands on /inicio (default) instead of /reset-password. Not run end to end on staging.
  • The 1376 status is not reset when a period is re-imported with replace (only declaracion is), so a 1376 can stay generada over new lines.
  • Recomputation drift: PADI files are not stored and plan or mapping edits do not reset statuses, so a period marked generada can produce a different file later.
  • updated_at on declaracion and declaracion_1376 has no trigger and is never set by the code, so "last update" on the dashboard likely stays at the creation time.
  • empresa.estado, responsable and ultimo_movimiento are never written; every company shows as "Pendiente".
  • declaracion.estado = con_errores is allowed by the CHECK and never written or displayed.
  • The 1376 line catalog (codigo_linea_1376) is a provisional seed built from a user spreadsheet (DJ 1376.xlsx), because the official DGI code list had not been captured. The PADI 1376 export relies on these codes and their meaning.
  • Both unique constraints on plan_cuentas ignore declaracion, so an account or IVA code cannot be shared by a 2181 row and a 1376 row of one company (inferred; UI behaviour not run).
  • The 1376 review page inserts a row while rendering (a GET with a write), and the statuses are updated from the browser with plain UPDATEs, so correctness of statuses relies on RLS alone.
  • Sidebar rate fallback: resolverCotizacionBcu reads the cache with maybeSingle() filtered only by currency, but since 2026-07-28 the table stores one row per day. With more than one cached day the query errors, so the "last available value" fallback likely never shows and the card shows the error state when BCU is down. Not reproduced.
  • Resend sender onboarding@resend.dev is a shared test sender; delivery to customers is unverified.

Not in scope of this map

  • API endpoint contracts (business-api-context), user journeys (business-e2e-context) and the vocabulary of domain terms (business-domain-context).
  • Subscription plans: the landing shows example plans and a 14-day trial, but no table stores a plan, price or subscription.
  • Declarations 2183 and 1050 are shown as disabled options and have no tables or code.
